haiku-low.q1: Captured amount minus the sum of pending and succeeded refund amounts. Failed refunds are excluded. The admin page shows this as remaining_cents, for display only.
haiku-low.q2: It retries up to 3 more times, 4 attempts total, with backoff and jitter, using the same idempotency key. If all fail, the refund stays pending and reconciliation takes over.
haiku-low.q3: The refund is marked failed through applyRefundTransition, with provider_error stored. There are no retries and no customer email.
haiku-low.q4: A refund becoming succeeded through applyRefundTransition, which writes one email_outbox row. A worker then sends the email.
haiku-low.q5: Only succeeded refunds count. Above 0 but below captured is Partially refunded, equal to captured is Refunded, and 0 leaves it unchanged. It updates in the same transaction as the refund change.
haiku-low.q6: The step 4 transaction locks the payment row with SELECT FOR UPDATE. The second admin waits, then sums the first pending row and is rejected if the total is too high.
haiku-low.q7: It is refunds.id, which is the browser's refund_request_id. It is stored in refunds.idempotency_key at insert and reused on every create retry.
haiku-low.q8: Each event_id is inserted once into refund_webhook_events in the same transaction. Changes happen only from pending, so repeats are no-ops and conflicts are audited and alerted. Email uses a unique refund_id and type constraint.
haiku-low.q9: It stays pending with no provider_refund_id, not failed, because the provider may have created the refund. Audit refund.submit_exhausted is written and reconciliation takes over.
haiku-low.q10: A job runs every 15 minutes. It retrieves refunds with a provider id hourly. Succeeded or failed applies that status, and other answers leave it pending. Refunds without an id are re-sent or looked up by metadata.
haiku-low.q11: The message "Refund submitted, awaiting provider confirmation", plus the refund id, amount and pending status. The browser does not wait for the provider.

sonnet.q1: Captured amount minus the sum of amount_cents of that payment's refunds with status pending or succeeded (failed ones excluded). This is remaining_cents, shown for display only; the authoritative check is done under a row lock in step 4.
sonnet.q2: The refund stays pending. It is retried up to 3 more times (4 attempts total) with backoff and jitter, each attempt claiming first, using the same idempotency key and a 10s timeout; the last error is stored in provider_error. A 2xx on any attempt goes to step 7 and a 4xx goes to step 8. If all fail, it stays pending with no provider_refund_id (not marked failed), refund.submit_exhausted is audited, and step 10 reconciliation takes over.
sonnet.q3: The refund is marked failed via applyRefundTransition(pending to failed, source provider_response), with the provider's message stored in provider_error and audited. No retries and no customer email. The amount is released automatically because failed refunds are excluded from the sum. The admin sees the provider's message (escaped) on the refund list. The order status does not change.
sonnet.q4: The refund becoming succeeded. applyRefundTransition writes an email_outbox row (one per refund) in the same transaction; the email worker then polls for unsent rows (sent_at IS NULL) and sends the email. Failed refunds get no email.
sonnet.q5: It is based on succeeded refunds only. Sum 0 means the label is unchanged; above 0 but below the captured amount means Partially refunded; equal to the captured amount means Refunded. Pending and failed refunds are ignored. It is recomputed and stored in payments.refund_status in the same transaction when a refund becomes succeeded (inside applyRefundTransition).
sonnet.q6: In step 4's transaction, the payment row is locked with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, so concurrent refunds on that payment wait. The second admin then sums pending and succeeded refunds, including the first's pending row, and is rejected (audited, rolled back) if sum plus the requested amount exceeds the captured amount.
sonnet.q7: The idempotency key is the refund id, which equals the browser-generated refund_request_id (UUID). It is stored in the refunds row's idempotency_key column (idempotency_key = id) when the row is inserted in step 4, and every attempt, retry and reconciliation re-send uses the same key.
sonnet.q8: Duplicates: each event is inserted into refund_webhook_events with a unique event_id in the same transaction as the change; a repeated event_id returns 200 and does nothing. Out of order: applyRefundTransition only allows a change from pending and terminal statuses never change. If the refund is already terminal and the event agrees it is a no-op; if it conflicts nothing changes, conflicting_event is audited and an alert is raised. The email outbox has a unique (refund_id, type) constraint, and the outbox row is only written when the transition to succeeded happens.
sonnet.q9: It stays pending, with no provider_refund_id. It is not marked failed because the provider may have actually created the refund. The refund.submit_exhausted audit is written, and step 10 takes over.
sonnet.q10: The reconciliation job (step 10), scheduled every 15 minutes. With a provider_refund_id and at least 1 hour since the last check (last_status_check_at, or created_at if none), it calls the provider's retrieve API: succeeded calls applyRefundTransition to succeeded, failed calls it to failed (source reconciliation), any other answer leaves it pending. Without a provider id and created under 2 hours ago, it re-sends the create call on every run with the same key (up to 4 attempts, same claim). At 2 hours or older it never re-sends but looks the refund up by our metadata refund id via the provider's search/list call; if found it stores the id and applies the status, if not it leaves it pending. last_status_check_at is updated after any call that got an answer.
sonnet.q11: "Refund submitted, awaiting provider confirmation", showing the refund id, amount and pending status. The browser does not wait for the provider.
